dialog: User: Hello! I hope you're doing well. I wanted to talk about "The Ides of March" since I didn't enjoy it. The movie was quite boring, especially because I'm not into politics. The storyline didn't capture my interest. I wouldn't recommend it to anyone who isn't a fan of political movies.

Agent: I understand your viewpoint. If you're not into politics, "RocknRolla" might not be the best choice for you either. It has its moments, but overall, it can be a bit dull. The intricate plotlines and fancy camera work might not make up for the lack of engaging storytelling.
User: Thanks for the heads up. I'll pass on "RocknRolla" as well.

Agent: I have another recommendation for you. You might enjoy "Scrooged." It's a modern-day Christmas classic featuring Bill Murray as a rotten television executive in a retelling of "A Christmas Carol." It's a fun and heartwarming holiday movie with just the right amount of sassiness.
User: That sounds interesting! I'll give "Scrooged" a try.
Agent: Great! If you ever need more movie recommendations, feel free to ask. I'm here to help.
User: Thanks, I appreciate your assistance.
Agent: You're welcome! Enjoy watching "Scrooged" and have a great day!
User: Hello! I see you didn't like "Veep: Season 1". Can you tell me more about it?

Agent: Sure! I'll tell you what... HBO has done it again! With only an eight episode first season, Veep has got my vote! The show is funny, witty, well acted, and at the end of each short 30-minute episode I'm left wishing the show was an hour. The good news: Veep has been picked up for a second season according to a 4/30/2012 Hollywood Reporter article. Like The Office, the show is shot in that improv, hand-held camera, 'you are there' style of filming, which for me can get a little annoying (especially since filming in that style has been an epidemic of late), but that is the show's only negative in my opinion. The show follows VP Selina Meyer and her bumbling staff as they try to navigate through the brutal behind the scenes world of Washington DC politics. And for the most part poor Selina and her staff find themselves in wayyyy over their heads in almost every situation. The result is the hilariousness that ensues as we watch Selina get herself into one embarrassing and humiliating situation after another, then try to get out of those situations without self destructing. And don't get me wrong about the "bumbling staff" comment... I mean...
User: That sounds interesting! Can you recommend something similar?

Agent: Of course! I think you might like "Corazon de Caballero". It's a fun movie with a predictable plot but with lots of exciting jousting action and plenty of humor. Among other little jokes, jousts are announced like modern boxing matches, and the accompanying songs and dances are from a few hundred years ahead of medieval times. Heath Ledger reminds us how sorry we are to see him go so young, but at least we have Rufus Sewell still around. Worth watching.
User: Great, I'll give it a shot without any reason.
Agent: Perfect! If you need any more recommendations, feel free to ask.
User: Thank you, but I'm good for now. I appreciate your help!
Agent: You're welcome! If you have any more questions in the future, feel free to ask. Have a great day!
